notes: Small money, but realistic odds and a good resume line for college applications. Rules PDF linked from the page.

eligibility: Graduating high school seniors who will major in music; performance (not composition); $20 fee; NFMC membership.
notes: Only if he performs at a strong level on his instrument.

eligibility: SCI student member; high schoolers eligible if studying privately with a professional composer.
notes: Page shows a 2020 deadline; email the coordinator before relying on it. More useful once he is in college.

name: USC Merit Scholarships (incl. Thornton)
amount: A few thousand dollars up to full tuition; 1,000+ students got $10k+/yr last year
eligibility: Admitted USC applicants who apply by Dec 1; Thornton portfolio counts toward consideration.
notes: Dec 1 is the same as the Thornton composition deadline, so applying on time is the whole application. Odds are low at a 3.4 for the big academic awards; a strong portfolio is his real lever.

name: Chapman University merit + Hall-Musco Conservatory music scholarship
amount: Merit up to $42,000/yr; music talent awards extra (stackable)
eligibility: All admitted applicants considered automatically; music awards come from the Creative Supplement and audition. Music award renewal needs a 3.0 Chapman GPA.
notes: One of the best bets: merit is automatic and music talent awards stack with it. Apply Early Action for best money.

name: University of Redlands Achievement Award + Conservatory Music Award
amount: Achievement Award up to $37,000/yr; Music Award up to $10,000/yr
eligibility: All applicants considered for Achievement Award. Music Award needs a separate Conservatory application and audition. Renewal needs a 3.0 GPA.
notes: Strong fit for a 3.4 student: Redlands discounts heavily. Apply to the Conservatory at the same time as the university.

name: University of the Pacific Academic Merit + Conservatory Merit
deadline: Not posted; apply by Pacific's admission deadline
eligibility: Admitted students considered automatically; no FAFSA needed for merit. Conservatory merit based on audition/interview.
notes: Good fit; merit is holistic, not a hard GPA cutoff. Pacific also has an application fee waiver request form.

name: CalArts Merit Scholarship
eligibility: All admitted students considered; based on portfolio, not grades.
notes: Portfolio-driven, so his GPA matters little here.

name: Berklee merit / full-tuition scholarships
amount: Partial up to full tuition; Presidential covers full cost (very few)
eligibility: All applicants considered automatically from audition and interview; composition materials can be included.
notes: Audition-driven, no GPA lever.

name: University of Cincinnati CCM talent + National Outreach Award
amount: National Outreach $10,000/yr (out-of-state); Cincinnatus avg ~$2,000/yr; CCM talent awards cover tuition portions
deadline: 2026-11-01 to be safe (UC admissions page says Nov 1; CCM page says Dec 1)
eligibility: CCM applicants auto-considered for talent awards from prescreen/audition; National Outreach for non-OH/IN/KY freshmen.
notes: The two UC Cincinnati pages disagree on the academic-award deadline, so treat Nov 1 as the real one.

name: Oberlin Conservatory Dean's Award + Oberlin Commitment Scholarship
amount: Commitment $10,000/yr for all enrolling; Dean's Award varies
eligibility: All admitted conservatory students reviewed automatically; Dean's Award from audition and ensemble needs.
notes: Automatic.

eligibility: Awarded at admission based on academics; renewal needs 3.0.

amount: 40+ named awards, $400,000+/yr, partial to full tuition
deadline: Beach Scholarships portal, fall awards apply Jan-Mar 2027

name: UCSB Department of Music audition scholarships
eligibility: Incoming music majors; awarded from audition results; no separate application.
notes: Automatic with the BM application.

eligibility: Scholarship committee reviews admitted music majors; some named awards are for incoming freshmen (Dean's Recognition - Freshman).
notes: Several listed awards also require need; ask the department which are merit-only.

eligibility: Pass the entrance audition first; university application asks for financial need.
notes: Low expected value for this family because need is part of the process.

eligibility: Based on academic excellence, financial need and intent to enroll.
